focus: Consolidation: merge cost of push-to-main workflows — per-job billing, rebuild-commit multiplier, shared setup, changed-files gate, required-check names and the README contract

graphEvents.label: Rebuild commits are 48% of push SHAs and re-run 13 workflows
paths-ignore on generated files is the top consolidation lever

label: 35 of 73 distinct push SHAs (47.9%) are trigger-index rebuild commits; each re-runs 13 downstream workflows, costing ~2030 billed min in the 23.5h window (~2074/day, 54% of the 3812/day estimate).
Merging workflows with parallel jobs is cost-neutral: billing is the sum over jobs of ceil(job seconds/60), so the same N jobs bill the same whether they live in one file or N files.

11 workflows install in two or more jobs (spec-kit-check 9 installs, routing-registry-drift 4, four at 3, five at 2) and no workflow uses actions/cache or setup-node cache — the duplication a consolidation should target is job-level installs, not workflow files.

Merging the nine always-run workflows into one job would save an inferred 700–900 billed min/day by removing 8 duplicated checkouts/setups/installs and 8 ceil roundings, at the cost of nine check names, their failure isolation and the README's per-workflow trigger rows.

No reusable workflow or composite action exists (zero uses: ./ hits); a workflow_call callee bills the same minutes, so a composite setup action inlined into existing jobs is the only shared form that can also carry a cache without changing job names.

A single changed-files gate is worse than native paths: filters — a non-matching path-filtered workflow bills 0 while a gate job bills at least 1 min per run, and it depends on the unresolved skipped-required-check question.

The README (one responsibility row and one trigger/why row per workflow) and the external branch-ruleset required-check list are the two contracts a merge breaks; check-gate-inputs.sh reads workflows as text and gate-inputs enforces .opencode/.skilled path parity.

paths-ignore on the four generated index files across the 13 downstream workflows is the highest-saving, lowest-blast-radius consolidation: it removes 455 runs per window (~2074 billed min/day) without touching jobs, check names or triggers, and the rebuild's direct push proves the token already bypasses the ruleset.

direction: Merge workflows into fewer files with parallel jobs to save runner minutes
reason: Billing is per job; a merged file keeps every job and every ceil, so billed minutes are unchanged (F18-2).

direction: A single changed-files gate job replacing native paths filters
reason: Native path filters cost 0 when not matched; a gate job costs >=1 min per run and reintroduces the unresolved skipped-required-check question (F18-6).

direction: A shared reusable workflow (workflow_call) as a cost lever
reason: Callee jobs still provision their own runner, checkout and install; it dedupes YAML only (F18-5).
